children: Piccadily Agro Industries Limited reported a 19 per cent year-on-year rise in total income to ₹278.9 crore for the second quarter ended September 30, 2026, driven by strong growth in its distillery business. However, profit after tax fell 9 per cent to ₹24.2 crore compared to ₹26.6 crore in the same period last year, as higher finance and depreciation costs weighed on the bottom line.

The company’s distillery division, which includes its flagship Indri single malt whisky brand, grew revenue 30.5 per cent year-on-year to ₹271.3 crore and now accounts for 97.6 per cent of total operating revenue, up from 89.3 per cent a year ago. Branded alcobev volumes, covering Indri, Camikara, Cashmir and Whistler, grew 38 per cent year-on-year in Q2 and 45 per cent in the first half of FY27. EBITDA for Q2 rose 9.5 per cent to ₹53 crore, though the margin narrowed by 110 basis points to 21.7 per cent.

For the first half of FY2026-27, total income came in at ₹552.5 crore, up 19.1 per cent year-on-year, while EBITDA stood at ₹100.3 crore, up 14.5 per cent. Half-year PAT was nearly flat at ₹46 crore against ₹45.5 crore a year ago.

Finance costs in Q2 jumped 78.5 per cent to ₹11.6 crore, while depreciation rose 67.7 per cent to ₹10.4 crore, both reflecting the commissioning of expanded capacity at the Indri facility in Haryana and a new 200 KLPD distillery at Mahasamund in Chhattisgarh. Management noted that revenue realisation from the Chhattisgarh facility is expected from Q3 onwards. The sugar division, which is being demerged, saw revenues fall 73.4 per cent to ₹6.6 crore.

In October 2026, CRISIL assigned the company an A+/Stable rating for long-term and A1 for short-term bank facilities of ₹400 crore. The company currently has 96,000 barrels under maturation and is present across 33 countries.

Shares of Piccadily Agro were trading at ₹550.75 on the NSE on Monday afternoon, down 0.35 per cent on the day, and are trading about 32 per cent below their 52-week high of ₹809.70 touched in August 2026. The day high was at ₹566.00 and low at ₹545.50.

title: Piccadily Agro posts 19% revenue growth in Q2 FY27, shares trade flat
